claim: AUDIT section 2 item 2 sequel: is there a scale-free (decimal) correspondence between the Riemann zeros and the finite-disk spectrum, once the growing magnitudes are normalized into [0,1] decimals?

setup.zeros_source: mpmath.zetazero 1..100 (matches the 15 in Universals/spectral_analysis.py RIEMANN_ZEROS to ~1e-7)

zeros_decimalized.note: the zeros are a GUE (beta=2) system, so GOE 0.5307 is the wrong ensemble reference; this is why the earlier re-test only ever quoted the disk against GOE

rvm_residual.note: the decimal residual of the Riemann-von Mangoldt law (the S-term) stays < 1 over the first 100 zeros; consistent with the known |S(t)|=O(log t) bound but NOT a test of RH

verdict: DECIMAL PERSPECTIVE, NO SHARED SPECTRUM: (a) ensemble placement on the decimal axis: zeros are GUE (<r>=0.6108 ~ 0.5996, z=+0.58; GOE excluded at +4.14 sigma), the disk is Poisson (<r>=0.3738 ~ 0.3863, z=-0.43); (b) the two normalized spectra are NOT the same: KS p=3.0e-07; (c) the zeros' decimals are rigid (residual std 0.225, -3.01 sigma below random decimals), the disk's are at the random level (1.997, -0.88 sigma) - the zeros sit ~8.9x closer to the ideal grid than the disk (ratio 0.113); the Riemann-von Mangoldt residual over the first 100 zeros (max 0.9979 < 1) stays within its O(log t) bound - consistent with the known S-term bounds, NOT a test of RH (100 zeros cannot probe RH).
